principles.bounded_work: Large logical totals cross bounded pages, segments, or restartable work steps; a carrier bound does not redefine the logical total.
principles.configuration: Hardware- or environment-dependent limits that observably affect accepted work are operator-configurable and source-linked.
principles.implementation_privacy: Buffers, provider mechanics, database layout, and other non-observable implementation extents are not frozen here.
principles.logical_totals: A finite logical total has no product-level semantic maximum unless its owning contract declares one.
principles.operational_capacity: Capacity policy may explicitly reject, defer, or throttle work, but must not silently truncate it or become an undocumented semantic ceiling.

bounded-segment/v1.completion: the owner-declared progression or repeated-work contract

captureEvent.description: Observation Activity/PREMIS Event that used a file state and technical environment to generate provenance assertions. It does not generate the file state.

checkpointBody.description: A cumulative checkpoint over exact RFC 7464 bytes through the preceding entry. Tail truncation is detectable only when a checkpoint or tail digest is anchored externally.

contentDescription.description: Opaque primary byte-stream observations only: length and cryptographic fixity. Internal format, codec, dimensions, duration, and other byte semantics are outside the core profile.

correctionBody.description: Monotonic correction of prior assertion entries. Supersession changes the effective provenance description; it never denotes a change to the file itself.

coverage.description: Exhaustiveness status for every filesystem capture category. Complete concerns accountable enumeration under the declared plan, not universal retention.

digest.description: A cryptographic digest assertion. Content digests identify byte equality evidence, not file-entity identity.

entryReference.description: Reference to the exact UTF-8 JSON-text octets of an earlier journal entry, excluding RFC 7464 RS/LF framing.

environment.description: Host/OS/filesystem/runtime state used by an observation or transition; a PROV Entity, not an Agent merely because execution occurred there.

fileLineage.description: An abstract continuing file lineage. Each immutable state is a specialization of one lineage; grouping is an attributable continuity assertion, not inferred from path or digest alone.

fileState.description: One immutable, full observed snapshot of one operating-system regular-file state; a PROV Entity and PREMIS File.

graphFragment.description: An immutable atomic bundle of graph assertions. Arrays are semantic sets; array order does not imply chronology or causality.

text_role.description: Required when text and bytes coexist.

nativeMetadata.description: Source-native metadata evidence separated from any interpretation and from restoration semantics.

payloadBinding.description: Append-only assertion binding a journal state to a payload locator relative to the sidecar. The latest effective event per role determines the current binding.

processEvidence.description: Evidence supporting the asserted process type. Activity labels such as transcode are process provenance, never inferred from payload bytes unless explicitly marked as a comparison-based inference.

semanticAssertion.description: URI-named semantic assertion over the closed typed-value union. It cannot redefine core Riverhog provenance semantics.

transitionActivity.description: A real-world Activity/PREMIS Event that used, generated, or invalidated file states. It is distinct from observation capture.

utcDateTime.description: RFC 3339 date-time normalized to UTC with uppercase Z and at most nanosecond precision.

compatibility.archive: A valid v1 archive remains independently recoverable throughout the supported v1 lifetime. Pack construction, ingress checkpointing, and resumable-write strategies are not archive-format compatibility promises.
compatibility.cli: Command names, options, exit status, and structured output remain backward compatible throughout v1; prose output is for people.
compatibility.components: A supported deployment runs components from one coordinated product version.
compatibility.configuration: Accepted v1 configuration remains valid throughout v1 unless an unsafe value must be rejected.
compatibility.durable_state: Every later v1 release applies each durable-state authority's declared transition rule to state created by every earlier v1 release; this does not promise downgrade support or earlier software reading later state.
compatibility.http_api: Published v1 HTTP and native lifecycle-event contracts remain backward compatible throughout v1.
compatibility.licensing: Each continuing first-party Python distribution and OCI repository published in v1 retains every SPDX license alternative granted when that coordinate first shipped in v1; withdrawing a baseline grant requires a new major version.
compatibility.python_api: Freeze-protected declared public-module exports, callable signatures, selected constants, enum members and values, and selected public model and dataclass structures remain backward compatible throughout v1.
compatibility.recovery: Every later v1 recovery release reads every valid earlier v1 archive and provenance set.

policy.image_identity_scope: Runtime descriptors use OCI ImageID (the image configuration SHA-256 digest). A platform-specific image-manifest digest pins a deployed image; an image-index digest identifies the publication set, including attestations. Nonpublishing qualification records local ImageIDs; publication evidence records platform manifest digests. Per-release identities are not permanent v1 contract constants.
policy.platform_scope: A platform or architecture claim applies only to the exact published image, distribution, or installation form that carries it. Qualification platforms remain evidence unless an external contract independently protects them.
policy.role_retention: Publication creates no new product, API, protocol, provider, or direct-consumption promise. Each publication unit retains its exact release role and links to its existing semantic owners.
